recipes.name: S’mores from Scratch
recipes.summary: Homemade marshmallows, chocolate and graham crackers, toasted over a campfire or under the oven broiler. Plus a restaurant-style plate for a special night.
equipment: or a baking sheet lined with foil (broiler)
kitchen torch (optional, for the plated version)

ingredients.prep: homemade or store-bought, broken in half

steps: Campfire: let the fire burn down to glowing coals. Put a marshmallow on a long stick and hold it a few inches above the coals, turning slowly, until golden all over, 1 to 2 minutes. (If it catches fire, blow it out; some people like it charred.)
Set a square of chocolate on half a graham cracker, slide the hot marshmallow on top, cap with the other half, and pull out the stick. Wait a minute; the marshmallow is very hot.
Broiler: move a rack 4 to 6 inches below the broiler and heat it. Lay 8 cracker halves on the foil-lined sheet and top each with chocolate and a marshmallow.
Broil 30 seconds to 2 minutes, watching the whole time, until the marshmallows are puffed and golden. Cap with the other cracker halves and press gently.

Restaurant-style plate: heat the cream until it steams, pour it over 2 oz of the chopped chocolate, and stir into a smooth ganache. Swoosh a spoonful across each plate, crumble a graham cracker over it, stand two marshmallows on top, and brown them with a kitchen torch. Finish with a few flakes of salt.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the marshmallows, chocolate and graham crackers days ahead; they keep for weeks.
recipes.kids: A grown-up should supervise the fire and the broiler and work the torch. Teach kids to toast slowly above the coals, keep the stick pointed away from people, and let the marshmallow cool before biting.

swaps.vegetarian: Marshmallows are made with gelatin, usually from pork or beef. For vegetarian s’mores, use store-bought marshmallows labeled gelatin-free.
swaps.milk_chocolate: Use milk chocolate, homemade (see the chocolate recipe’s note) or store-bought.
